meta.title: Sofatap · Your phone, your living-room remote
meta.description: Sofatap turns your iPhone or Android phone into a touchpad and a voice-and-text keyboard for the Windows, Mac or Linux computer connected to your TV. Open source.

hero.eyebrow: For the computer on your TV
hero.title: Your phone, your living‑room remote.
hero.lead: Sofatap turns your iPhone or Android phone into a touchpad and a voice-and-text keyboard for the Windows, Mac or Linux computer connected to your TV. The picture stays on the big screen. You stay on the sofa.
hero.note: Open source · Windows, Mac and Linux
how.title: The whole screen is your touchpad
how.lead: One large rounded touch surface, with the keyboard and microphone close at hand. A calm field of mint dots bends under your finger, and taps send out a ripple.
how.alt: The Sofatap iPhone screen: a dark rounded surface filled with small mint dots, the logo and a QR-scan icon at the top, and keyboard and microphone buttons at the bottom.
gesture.hold.result: Drag, until you lift your finger
type.title: Type without getting up
type.lead: Search for a film, fill in a form or reply to a message. In supported fields, what you type or say reaches the computer as you go; elsewhere, you check a draft on the phone and then send it.
type.step1.title: Tap the microphone
type.step1.body: It only listens after you start dictation. When your iPhone and language support it, speech is recognized on the phone itself, and Sofatap doesn’t upload your audio. On Android, dictation uses the phone’s installed speech service, which decides how your audio is handled.
type.step2.title: Live, or as a draft
type.step2.body: Supported text fields on Windows and Mac update live as you type or dictate; other fields, Linux and older receivers use a draft and Send. You can also use system dictation or a third-party keyboard; third-party services handle data under their own terms.
type.step3.title: Send the draft
type.step3.body: For a draft, tap Send to type it into the field that’s focused on the computer. Sofatap never adds an extra Enter or submit, but line breaks in your text are typed too, and some fields treat a line break as Enter.
type.keyboard: When a compatible computer reports that you’ve clicked into a text field, the phone keyboard can open on its own. This depends on the app exposing standard accessibility information, which not every app does, so the keyboard button is always there too.
setup.title: Set up once, then sit back
setup.step1.title: Install the computer app
setup.step1.body: Download the receiver for Windows, Mac or Linux. It opens a small window with a QR code.
setup.step2.title: Use the same home network
setup.step2.body: Connect the phone and computer to the same home network. Guest Wi-Fi that keeps devices apart may block the connection.
setup.step3.title: Scan the code and allow control
setup.step3.body: Open Sofatap on your phone and scan the code in the computer’s window. If the computer asks, allow Sofatap to control it, for example Accessibility on a Mac or the remote-control permission prompt on Linux with Wayland. Until then, pairing alone can’t move the pointer.
privacy.title: Stays in your home
privacy.network: Phone and computer talk directly over your home network, encrypted with TLS and a pinned certificate. There’s no relay server in between.
privacy.mic: The microphone turns on only when you start dictation.
privacy.send: In live editing, a supported field changes as you type or dictate. With a draft, nothing is typed on the computer until you tap Send.
privacy.code: The pairing code gives control of your computer, so keep it to yourself.
download.title: Get Sofatap
download.lead: Sofatap needs the app on your iPhone or Android phone and a small receiver app on the computer. All are beta software.
platform.iphone.source: Build the iPhone app from source
platform.android.name: Android phone or tablet
platform.android.req: Android 8.0 (API 26) or later · direct APK, not from Google Play
platform.android.note: Beta. Updates are installed by hand over the existing app. The app is in English, Simplified Chinese and Japanese. Dictation uses the speech service installed on the phone, which decides how your speech is processed. Testing with real computers and TVs continues.
download.preview: On iPhone, use the app 1.0 (15) or later. We recommend updating both the phone and the computer to the latest version.
platform.windows.name: Windows
platform.windows.note: Beta. Not Authenticode-signed, so Windows may show an unknown publisher. Extract the whole zip and run SofaTap.exe. Allow network access only on your trusted home network.
platform.mac.name: Mac
platform.mac.req: macOS 15 or later · Apple Silicon or Intel · Notarized by Apple
platform.mac.note: Beta. Live editing on a Mac and input on Intel Macs haven’t been tested on real hardware yet.
platform.linux.name: Linux
platform.linux.req: x64 or ARM64 · GTK 3 · X11, with experimental Wayland
platform.linux.note: Beta. Install the system packages listed in the setup guide first. Linux uses a draft and Send; live editing isn’t available there yet. Wayland support is experimental, and input on a physical Linux desktop hasn’t been tested for this release.
platform.androidtv.name: Android TV (experimental)
platform.androidtv.req: Android 8.0 (API 26) or later · iPhone app 1.0 (20) or later, or the Android app
platform.androidtv.note: Experimental beta. Not yet accepted on household TVs or in third-party apps: Xiaomi and Sony pairing and text in YouTube, Netflix and browsers are unverified. TV keys need Android TV Remote Service enabled; select the Sofatap keyboard on the TV for text.
faq.title: Questions
faq.screen.q: Do I see the computer’s screen on my phone?
faq.screen.a: No. The computer stays connected to your TV as usual, and you watch the big screen. Sofatap only sends pointer, scroll and text input from your phone.
faq.network.q: Does it work over Bluetooth or the internet?
faq.network.a: Neither. The phone and computer connect directly over your home network, so both need to be on the same network.
faq.enter.q: Will it press Enter or submit forms by itself?
faq.enter.a: Not on its own. Sofatap never adds an Enter or a submit. Line breaks you include are part of your text, though, and some fields treat a line break as Enter, which can send a message or submit a form.
faq.keyboard.q: Does the keyboard pop up in every app?
faq.keyboard.a: Only for text fields that the app makes visible through accessibility information on a compatible receiver. Some apps, games and custom web widgets don’t, and on Linux this needs an optional accessibility component. You can always open the keyboard yourself.
faq.tv.q: Can it control a smart TV directly?
faq.tv.a: Sofatap is made for a computer connected to your TV. The iPhone app also has experimental previews for LG webOS and Android/Google TV; the Android app can control the experimental Android/Google TV receiver, but not LG webOS. No TV model has been qualified yet.
faq.plans.a: Manual control is free: touch, the keyboard and basic voice-to-text.
faq.ready.q: Is Sofatap ready for everyday use?
faq.ready.a: Not yet. It’s beta software: the iPhone app is in an open public beta, the Android app is a beta APK, and acceptance testing on real computers continues. Expect rough edges, and please report problems on GitHub.

demo.title: Try it: the phone moves the pointer on the TV
demo.hint: Move over the phone screen and the pointer moves on the TV. Click or tap once to select a film. Double-click or double-tap for a right click, then choose Play.
demo.hint.type: To search, click the search box on the TV, tap the keyboard button on the phone, type, then tap Send. This search box uses the draft-and-Send flow.
demo.keys: Keyboard: focus the phone screen, move the pointer with the arrow keys, press Enter to click and Shift+F10 or the Menu key to right-click. Escape closes the menu.
demo.tv: The TV shows a computer’s film library with nine films. The result of each gesture is announced in the status line.
demo.s.ready: Ready. The pointer is on the TV.
demo.s.clear: Left click on an empty area: nothing selected
demo.s.menuNone: Right click on an empty area. Point at a film to open its menu.
demo.s.demo: Demo playing. Touch the phone or press Stop to take over.
demo.s.done: Demo finished. Your turn: try it on the phone.
demo.s.field: Search box selected. Text you send from the phone goes here.
demo.s.compose: Phone keyboard open. Type, then tap Send.
demo.s.noField: Click the search box on the TV first, so the text has somewhere to go.
demo.s.heard: Dictated: {text}. Check it, then tap Send.
demo.s.mic: In the app, tap the microphone and speak: your words appear here as a draft to check before you send them.
